div.div: فَاغِيَةٌ and ↓ فَغْوٌ The flower of the حِنَّآء [i. e. Lawsonia inermis, or Egyptian privet]; (Fr, S, K;) as also فَاعِيَةٌ: (K in art. فعو or فعى:) or both signify the flower, or blossom, of anything [i. e. of any plant, or, app., of any fragrant plant: see Ham p. 713]: or, as is said in a trad., the فاغية is the prince, or chief, of the sweet-smelling plants of Paradise: Sh says that ↓ الفَغْوُ signifies نَوْر ورَائِحَة طَيِّبَة [a flower, or blossom; and a sweet odour: but I think that we should read نَوْرٌ ذُو رَائِحَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ a sort of flower, or blossom, having a sweet odour]: and IAar says that the فاغية is the best and the most fragrant of sweetsmelling plants: (TA:) or it is the flower produced by a branch of the حِنَّآء that has been planted inverted, and which is sweeter than [that of] the [common] حِنَّآء. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
